cards.label: Flamingo Lagoon
cards.challenge: Why do flamingos have long legs? Why stand on one?

video.title: Flamingo chicks at the Houston Zoo

cam.camLabel: Flamingo cam at the Houston Zoo

cards.printAnswer: Long legs let them wade and find food. Standing on one leg rests the other and can help them stay warm.

cards.label: Otter Creek
cards.challenge: Why do otters have whiskers? Why do they love water so much?

video.title: Otters in their habitat at the National Zoo

cam.camLabel: Otter cam at the Houston Zoo

cards.printAnswer: Whiskers feel fish moving in dark water. Otters hunt and play in water, and thick fur keeps them warm.

cards.label: Penguin Beach
cards.challenge: Why can’t penguins fly? Why the black-and-white coat?

video.title: African penguins at the San Diego Zoo

cam.camLabel: Penguin cam at the San Diego Zoo

cards.printAnswer: Their wings became flippers for swimming. Dark backs and white bellies help them hide from above and below.

cards.label: Hippo Pool
cards.challenge: Why does a hippo spend so much time in water? Can it really swim?

video.title: Hippos at the San Diego Zoo

cam.camLabel: Hippo cam at the San Diego Zoo

cards.printAnswer: Water keeps them cool and their skin safe from the sun. They mostly walk on the bottom — they are not strong swimmers.

cards.label: Giraffe Grove
cards.challenge: Why is a giraffe’s neck so long? How does it drink?

video.title: Giraffe calf at the Houston Zoo

cam.camLabel: Giraffe cam at the Houston Zoo

cards.printAnswer: A long neck reaches high leaves. To drink, a giraffe spreads its front legs and bends down carefully.

cards.label: Elephant Walk
cards.challenge: Why do elephants have huge ears? What is a trunk for?

video.title: Asian elephants at the National Zoo

cam.camLabel: Elephant cam at the Smithsonian National Zoo

cards.printAnswer: Big ears let heat out, like fans. The trunk smells, grabs food, drinks, and says hello.

cards.label: Lion Ridge
cards.challenge: Why does a lion have a mane? Why do they live in a pride?

cam.camLabel: Lion cam at the Smithsonian National Zoo

cards.printAnswer: A mane makes a lion look bigger and protects the neck. A pride is a family that hunts and raises cubs together.

cards.label: Tiger Trail
cards.challenge: Why does a tiger have stripes? Are they like a house cat?

video.title: Sumatran tigers at the San Diego Zoo Safari Park

cam.camLabel: Tiger cam at the San Diego Zoo Safari Park

cards.printAnswer: Stripes break up their shape in grass and shade. Yes — tigers are big cats in the same family as house cats.

cards.label: Gorilla Forest
cards.challenge: Why are gorillas so strong? Do they live in families?

cam.camLabel: Gorilla cam at the Houston Zoo

cards.printAnswer: Strong arms help them climb and pull plants. They live in family groups led by a silverback.

cards.label: Panda House
cards.challenge: Why do pandas eat bamboo? Why the black-and-white fur?

video.title: Giant panda Qing Bao in her habitat

cam.camLabel: Panda cam at the Smithsonian National Zoo

cards.printAnswer: Bamboo is almost all they eat, even though they are bears. The colors may help them hide or spot each other.

cards.label: Zebra yard
cards.challenge: Why does a zebra have stripes? Are any two the same?

video.title: Grant's zebras at the Houston Zoo

cards.printAnswer: Stripes may confuse flies and help zebras find their group. Each zebra’s pattern is a little different.

cards.label: Tortoise lawn
cards.challenge: Why do tortoises live so long? What’s the shell for?

video.title: Galapagos tortoise at the San Diego Zoo

cards.printAnswer: They grow slowly and some live more than 100 years. The shell is part of their body — armor they cannot crawl out of.

cards.label: Chimp grove
cards.challenge: Why do chimps use tools? How are they like us?

video.title: Chimpanzees at the Kansas City Zoo

cam.camLabel: Chimpanzee cam at the Houston Zoo

cards.printAnswer: They are smart and use sticks or rocks to get food. They have hands, faces, families, and feelings a lot like ours.

cards.label: Red panda perch
cards.challenge: Why isn’t a red panda a giant panda? Why the rusty fur?

video.title: Red panda at the San Diego Zoo

cam.camLabel: Red panda cam at the San Diego Zoo

cards.printAnswer: They are different animals — a red panda is more like a raccoon. Rusty fur helps it hide in trees.

cards.label: Lemur walk
cards.challenge: Why does a lemur have a striped tail? Why do they sit in the sun?

video.title: Ring-tailed lemurs at the Safari Park

cards.printAnswer: The tail is a flag so the group can follow. Morning sun warms them up after a cool night.

cards.label: Orangutan trail
cards.challenge: Why are orangutan arms so long? Why live in the trees?

video.title: Young orangutan at the San Diego Zoo

cam.camLabel: Ape cam at the San Diego Zoo

cards.printAnswer: Long arms are for swinging from branch to branch. Food and safety are up in the trees.

cards.label: Koala tree
cards.challenge: Why do koalas sleep so much? Why eat eucalyptus?

video.title: Baby koalas at the San Diego Zoo

cam.camLabel: Koala cam at the San Diego Zoo

cards.printAnswer: Eucalyptus leaves give little energy, so they sleep a lot. That plant is their food — most animals cannot eat it.
